title: Container Bookings: Standing of the Account on Which Late Document Entries Are Kept
content:
Late-document entries for shipping instructions on a Container Bookings booking are kept on the booking's charge account under two principles: one concerning the account of a booking the line has rolled, the other concerning the sequence of the late record.

## A rolled booking's account

Aurelia Hanse Line records a customer's lateness only against an account on which its own obligations to that customer for rolling the booking are fully booked. On a booking that the carrier has rolled, a late shipping-instruction entry stands correctly only where each carrier roll recorded on the booking already carries whatever compensation it earns under the product. Where a carrier roll earns nothing under the product, it leaves nothing to be booked.

## The sequence of the late record

The late record of a booking follows the sequence in which the documents reached the line. A shipping-instruction receipt that is already on file without its late entry is owed that entry from the moment of receipt, and the entry is written at the next handling of the booking. That entry belongs to the booking as it stands while those instructions are the latest document received on it, so that the late record lists late submissions in the order of arrival.

## Points of judgement

- **Does a customer roll affect the first principle?** No; it concerns only rolls the carrier caused.
- **Does the first principle change the amount of the late entry?** No; it concerns the account on which the entry is written, not its price.
- **Hypothetical case.** On an invented booking rolled once by the carrier under a product that pays nothing for carrier rolls, the roll earns no compensation, so the first principle asks nothing of the account.
